items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Tommy Newsom is a great writer, writes a lot for my band and I’m so blessed to have him.

ctx.x: Yeah well you have to, it’s a requirement in school, to learn how to play the piano. How when you go into a jazz program you have to take jazz piano as well. But I mean I’m horrible, I can’t play the piano, but I can play it as a writer. You know I can figure out my own chords and I can play through a passage like in slow motion until I learn it. And certainly I’ve studied harmony and theory, like inside out, enough to make you sick. But you know I started writing and this is also funny. Al Hamme, the person from…

the concert. And I went to several performances that day. And I could not stand any of it. And this is how stupid I was. I said, “that music is so horrible, I bet I could write something better than that.” So the first thing I wrote was this four movement suite for percussion and saxophone for Al. And we played it and it came out really good. So I was like well I can kind of do this too. I don’t mean it to sound, like that sounds like egomaniacal, but for some reason, I don’t mean it that way. I just was…
